title: Hyatt Property Catalog
skill:
# Hyatt — Property Catalog (curated, citation-stable)

> A **curated shortlist of real Hyatt properties in the major business-event cities**, organised by
> city and keyed to the convention/event venues that actually matter for a corporate group. The
> proposal page's *"Where you'll stay"* section (`stayCities`) is built by **selecting** from this
> file rather than researching hotels from scratch on every run — that is what makes the section
> fast, consistent, and citable. Scope is **corporate group booking**: room blocks around an event,
> crew and instructor stays, and executive/VIP rooms.
>
> **Concept-demonstration notice:** this file was authored for an Optimizely Opal POC and for
> account-based-marketing training. It is **not** an official communication of Hyatt Hotels
> Corporation, and pages built from it must carry the same disclaimer in their footer.
>
> **Integrity rule:** this is a *selection* list, not a facts list. Every property claim a page
> makes must appear in the page's `sources` array — group **`"hyatt"`** when the claim comes from
> Hyatt's own published property page, group **`"account"`** when it was verified live for this
> account (availability, rates, dates, capacity). Never render a property claim unsourced. Do
> **not** invent properties, room counts, meeting-space square footage, ratings or awards — none
> are in this file, and none may be added by inference. Distances here are deliberately
> **approximate and qualified** ("~10 min walk", "one stop on the Metro"); keep the `~` /
> "approximately" qualifier in the rendered copy. If a city you need has no Hyatt property listed
> below, say so plainly to the builder's own output and fall back to a **qualitative** statement
> ("Hyatt can place your delegation within the city's conference district") — never name a hotel
> to fill the gap.

---

## How to read an entry

Each city gives the **event venues that matter**, then 2–4 properties. Each property carries:

- **name** — as Hyatt brands it, plus its **brand family** (Hyatt Regency, Grand Hyatt, Park Hyatt,
  Andaz, Hyatt Place, Hyatt House, The Unbound Collection by Hyatt)
- **good for** — the group-booking job it does: large delegations, extended-stay crews,
  executive/VIP, receptions, cost-managed delegate rooms
- **near** — approximate, qualified proximity to a named venue
- **image / alt** — an image URL ready to drop into `stayCities[].cards[].image`

`verify live` on an entry means the property's current brand, name or status is the thing most
likely to have moved — confirm it on hyatt.com before it reaches a prospect, and cite it under
group `"account"`.

## image_note

Every image in this file is **externally hosted** and drops straight into a content field — the
layout treats an image as an opaque string, so an absolute `https://…` URL behaves exactly as a
local path does, with no upload step. External URLs are Wikimedia Commons `Special:FilePath` links
with an explicit `?width=`, which redirect to the CDN, survive filename-to-hash changes, and serve
a right-sized derivative instead of a multi-megabyte original.

**Every URL here was verified on 2026-08-10** — fetched live, HTTP 200, `image/jpeg`, and
pixel-measured. The measured size is printed beside each one. Re-verify anything you add, and never
write a URL you have not seen resolve: a broken image on a prospect page is worse than a plain one.

### The three honest categories

Each property entry says which of these its picture is, and its `Alt:` line is written to match.
**Copy the `Alt:` text verbatim** — it is worded to be true of the photograph:

- **a real photograph of this property** — the actual hotel, usually with signage legible. Best case.
- **the surrounding street or district, NOT the building** — used where no free photo of the hotel
  exists. Perfectly good on the page, *provided* the alt keeps saying it is the neighbourhood. Never
  re-word one of these to imply it shows the hotel.
- **none of its own** — no trustworthy photograph exists. The entry says so. Use the generic
  fallback below and describe the generic picture honestly.

Never illustrate one hotel with a photograph of a **different** hotel. A Grand Hyatt signboard over
a Hyatt House entry, or a competitor's flags on a building Hyatt now operates, is the exact error
this file exists to prevent — two candidate images were rejected on precisely that ground.

### Generic fallback set (ships in `public/assets/`)

For a property whose entry says **none of its own**, choose by what the property is good for:

| Good for | Use |
| --- | --- |
| executive / VIP, smaller sessions | `/assets/boardroom.jpg` |
| extended-stay crews, trainers, cost-managed delegate rooms | `/assets/guestroom.jpg` |
| receptions, networking, hospitality | `/assets/rooftop-networking.jpg` |
| classroom / training / bootcamp space | `/assets/classroom.jpg` |

Also available: `/assets/nyc-grand-hyatt-dusk.jpg`, `/assets/nyc-grand-hyatt-sign.jpg`,
`/assets/london-blackfriars-dusk.jpg`, `/assets/london-stratford-entrance.jpg` — these four show
**specific named properties**, so use them only for those properties, never as generic filler.
`/assets/hero-nyc-skyline.jpg` is **retired**: at 612x408 it was far too small for the full-bleed
hero it was being used for. Take heroes from the City hero images table instead.

### Attribution is not optional

Every external file here is Creative Commons and **all but the CC0 one require attribution**. Each
entry carries a `Credit:` line. Collect the credits for every external image you actually place and
list them in the page's `disclaimer` field, in the form
`Photography: <author> (<licence>) via Wikimedia Commons; <author> (<licence>); …`.
If you cannot credit an image, do not use it — one verified exterior was dropped from this catalog
for exactly that reason (CC BY-SA 3.0 with no recorded author).

### No picture twice in one city's row

Where two properties in a city would have shared a photograph, this file deliberately gives it to
one of them and marks the other **none of its own**. Repeating an image down a row of cards is the
fastest way to make a shortlist look invented.

---

## City hero images — for `heroImage`

**This is where `heroImage` comes from.** Look up the city the account's calendar leads with and
use its URL verbatim. The hero renders as a **full-bleed background across the entire viewport**,
so it must be one of these wide cityscapes — never an interior, never a property card image, and
never another city's skyline standing in.

Every URL below was fetched and measured on 2026-08-10: HTTP 200, `image/jpeg`, dimensions as
listed. All are freely licensed Wikimedia Commons files served through `Special:FilePath`, which
redirects to the CDN and survives filename-to-hash changes. Note Commons rounds `?width=` up to
its own derivative buckets, so the measured width is often larger than the number requested.

**If the lead city is not in this table, omit `heroImage` entirely.** The layout then renders a

## New York City

**Venues:** Jacob K. Javits Convention Center (West Side) · Hudson Yards · Midtown hotel-and-meeting
district around Grand Central.

- **Hyatt Grand Central New York** — *Hyatt Hotels brand* (the Grand Central flagship, formerly
  branded Grand Hyatt New York; *verify live* — the site is subject to a long-running redevelopment
  plan). Good for: **large delegations** who need one address everyone can find, and rail arrivals.
  Near: **~15 min by cab/subway to the Javits Center**, directly beside Grand Central Terminal.
  Image: `https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Hyatt_Grand_Central_New_York_%2854824182198%29.jpg?width=1000`
  Image shows: *a real photograph of this property* — 1280x2221px.
  Alt: "The bronze-glass exterior of Hyatt Grand Central New York on East 42nd Street beside Grand Central Terminal, with the Hyatt flag at street level"
  Credit: ajay_suresh / CC BY 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons) — **must be credited on the page**.
- **Hyatt House New York / Chelsea** — *Hyatt House*. Good for: **extended-stay crews**,
  instructors and production staff who arrive early and leave late; residential suites with
  kitchens. Near: **~10–15 min walk to the Javits Center**.
  Image: `https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/206-220_West_15th_Street.jpg?width=1000`
  Image shows: *the surrounding street or district, NOT the building* — 1280x1069px.
  Alt: "A row of red-brick townhouses on West 15th Street in Chelsea, Manhattan — the neighbourhood around the hotel, not the hotel itself"
  Credit: Beyond My Ken / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons) — **must be credited on the page**.
- **Hyatt Place New York / Midtown South** — *Hyatt Place*. Good for: **cost-managed delegate
  rooms** at volume without leaving Midtown. Near: **~15 min to the Javits Center**, walking
  distance to Penn Station.
  Image: **none of its own** — use the generic fallback for what this property is good for.
  Image note: No trustworthy free photograph of the building exists on Commons, and every nearby candidate was either a generic Midtown street or a landmark (Macy's, Herald Square) that would read as a different place. Use a local /assets fallback.
- **Andaz 5th Avenue** — *Andaz*. Good for: **executive/VIP** rooms and smaller
  character-led sessions opposite the New York Public Library. Near: **~20 min to the Javits
  Center**, on Fifth Avenue at 41st Street.
  Image: `https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/New_York_City%2C_Midtown_Manhattan%2C_New_York_Public_Library%2C_Stephen_A._Schwarzman_Building%2C_1897-1911._5th_Avenue_%282011%29.jpg?width=1000`
  Image shows: *the surrounding street or district, NOT the building* — 1280x853px.

  Credit: (vincent desjardins) from Paris, France / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons) — **must be credited on the page**.

> Also in market and safe to name if the brief calls for a top-end flagship: **Park Hyatt New
> York** (*Park Hyatt*, West 57th Street) — executive/VIP only; do not position it as a delegate
> block.

## Las Vegas

**Venues:** Sands Expo / The Venetian Expo · Las Vegas Convention Center · Mandalay Bay
Convention Center.

**Honest caveat — read before writing copy.** Hyatt does **not** operate a large
convention-anchor Hyatt Regency adjacent to the Sands Expo / Venetian, and this file will not
pretend otherwise. Select-service Hyatt properties (**Hyatt Place Las Vegas** and **Hyatt House Las
Vegas**, *Hyatt Place* / *Hyatt House* — *verify live*, both name and location) suit
**cost-managed delegate rooms and extended-stay crews**, at **approximately a short drive from the
Strip venues**. **Hyatt Regency Lake Las Vegas** (*Hyatt Regency*) is a resort option for an
off-Strip executive offsite, **approximately 30+ minutes out of town** — do not present it as
walkable to a convention centre.

If the brief needs a Strip-adjacent block, use the **qualitative** framing — Hyatt's team places
the delegation and manages the block — and cite nothing rather than name a hotel Hyatt does not run.
Image for either select-service card: `/assets/guestroom.jpg` — *local asset.*
Alt: "A Hyatt guestroom with a work desk, ready for a delegate arrival".

## Cities deliberately not covered

This catalogue is intentionally short of the full Hyatt footprint. If a prospect's event is in a
city not listed above, **do not extrapolate from a nearby city**. Either research that city's
Hyatt properties live and cite each one under group `"account"`, or write the qualitative
statement. A three-property city section that is accurate beats a five-property one that is
half-guessed.

## How the page builder uses this file

1. Read the account's **event calendar** from the research canvas and list the cities its events
   are actually in.
2. For each such city, look it up above and **select 2–3 properties** that match the account's
   **delegate profile** — one anchor for the bulk of the delegation, one for the crew/extended-stay
   or cost-managed rooms, and (only when the brief warrants it) one executive/VIP or reception
   property. Do not list every property in the city; the section is a curated recommendation, not
   an inventory.
3. Map each selection into a `stayCities` entry, exactly this shape:

   ```json
   {
     "city": "London",
     "pin": "Near the Barbican",
     "cards": [
       {
         "name": "Hyatt Regency London Blackfriars",
         "dist": "~10 min walk to the Barbican",
         "body": "One sentence in the account's own register on why this property fits this delegation.[^4]",
         "image": "/assets/london-blackfriars-dusk.jpg",
         "alt": "Hyatt Regency London Blackfriars facade at dusk"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

   `city` = the event city · `pin` = the venue the block is positioned against ("Near the Javits
   Center") · `name` = the property name **exactly** as written above · `dist` = the qualified
   proximity, `~` intact · `body` = the group-booking rationale in the account's vocabulary, not
   Hyatt's · `image` / `alt` = copied from the entry, external URL or local path.
4. **Cite every property.** Add a `sources` entry per named property — group `"hyatt"` for its
   published hyatt.com property page, group `"account"` for anything verified live (availability,
   dates, rates, status) — and put the matching `[^n]` marker in that card's `body`. A card with a
   named hotel and no source is a defect.
5. Keep every distance qualified, keep the brand family accurate, and if the city isn't here or the
   entry says *verify live* and you cannot verify it, drop the card rather than soften the claim.

> **External image URLs were checked on 2026-08-10** and returned HTTP 200: Andaz London
> Liverpool Street, Grand Hyatt Tokyo, Hyatt Regency San Francisco, Andaz Singapore, Park Hyatt
> Sydney. Any URL added later must be checked the same way — a dead link renders as a broken
> image on a page you are showing a prospect. When no URL verifies, use a `/assets/*.jpg` path
> and say in the alt text that it is representative rather than the property itself.
skill_sementics: Curated, citation-stable catalogue of real Hyatt properties in the major business-event cities, organised by city and keyed to the convention/event venues that matter: New York (Javits Center, Hudson Yards), London (Barbican, ExCeL), Chicago (McCormick Place), San Francisco (Moscone), Las Vegas (Sands Expo/Venetian, LVCC), Orlando (Orange County Convention Center), Boston (BCEC, Hynes), Amsterdam (RAI), Paris (Porte de Versailles, Palais des Congres, Villepinte), Germany (Messe Berlin, Messe Dusseldorf, and an explicit no-property note for Messe Frankfurt), Dubai (World Trade Centre, Expo City), Singapore (Marina Bay Sands, Suntec), Sydney (ICC Sydney), and Tokyo (Tokyo Big Sight, Makuhari Messe). Each entry gives the property name as Hyatt brands it, its brand family (Hyatt Regency, Grand Hyatt, Park Hyatt, Andaz, Hyatt Place, Hyatt House, The Unbound Collection by Hyatt), what it is good for in a group-booking context (large delegations, extended-stay crews, executive/VIP, receptions, cost-managed delegate rooms), an approximate qualified distance to the named venue, and an image URL plus alt text ready for the page's stayCities[].cards[].image field - externally hosted Wikimedia Commons Special:FilePath URLs where a trustworthy one exists, otherwise one of the nine local /assets/*.jpg paths. Use when building or editing the 'Where you'll stay' section of a Hyatt ABM proposal page so hotels are SELECTED from a curated list instead of researched ad hoc per run: pick 2-3 properties per event city based on the account's delegate profile, map them into stayCities, and cite every named property in the page's sources array (group "hyatt" for its published hyatt.com page, group "account" for anything verified live). Availability, capacity and exact distances change, so distances keep their "~"/approximately qualifier and no property, room count, square footage or award may be invented; if a city has no Hyatt property listed, fall back to a qualitative statement rather than naming one.
